where: Section 3, final check line ('a short stub is shorter than λ/4 when it supplies positive reactance')
problem: The check is worded for a series stub (reactance). The procedure just above is for a shunt stub, which adds susceptance, and there the rule reverses: a short-circuited shunt stub of length l < λ/4 gives B = −Y0·cot(βl) < 0, i.e. inductive (negative) susceptance. To supply positive susceptance the short stub must be longer than λ/4 (up to λ/2). A student following this check will pick the wrong stub length.
fix: State it per stub type: 'Check the answer: d must lie between 0 and λ/2. A short-circuited series stub gives X = Z0·tan(βl), so it is shorter than λ/4 when it supplies positive (inductive) reactance. A short-circuited shunt stub gives B = −Y0·cot(βl), so it is shorter than λ/4 when it supplies negative (inductive) susceptance, and lies between λ/4 and λ/2 when it supplies positive (capacitive) susceptance.'

problem: VSWR is used from the first paragraph but never expanded or defined, so a reader meeting the abbreviation for the first time has no full form to attach to the formula.
fix: At first use write: 'VSWR (voltage standing wave ratio, the ratio of maximum to minimum voltage on the line) becomes a circle.'
